reason: Verified the PR head (3d13c51, fetched as refs/pull/190/head) against a clean worktree rather than trusting the description. The diff vs origin/main is exactly the five claimed files at 193/-89, matching the case metadata; the head is a merge of main whose only incoming work is unrelated setup-wizard changes, with no conflict in any touched file. Gates re-run locally: cargo fmt --check clean, cargo clippy --all-targets clean, cargo test 812 passed / 0 failed. The change is render-only as claimed: header_line now reserves GAP + one glyph column before trimming so a narrow frame drops the label and the warning count instead of the status indicator; category_line puts the arrow at column 2 and the label at column 4, and DETAIL_INDENT (4) matches that label column, so detail rows nest under their parent instead of being outdented past it; append_inbox's removed leading spaces are consistent with the frame owning the single indent origin. Row counts per category are unchanged, so selected_row / scroll_offset / overseer_frame_height are untouched and the existing popup-anchor and scroll tests pass unmodified. All four pre-existing overseer_frame tests survive the module move with unchanged bodies, and the two new tests assert the geometry at both 24- and 48-column widths, so both regressions are pinned. The disclosed deviation from subtask #247 (4-column detail indent instead of 2) is sound: at a 4-column label position a 2-column indent would outdent the detail rows left of their own label, and 4 still satisfies the parent criterion of less than the previous 6. Two description inaccuracies, neither merge-blocking and neither introduced by this change: the checklist claim that source files are under the 300-line limit is wrong for src/ui/overseer/render.rs at 309 lines, but that file was already 307 on main and this PR adds only two comment lines to it; and the stated 807-test count is the branch-tip figure, now 812 at the merge commit because main added tests. Nothing here warrants a veto or a human escalation.
